thread.title: Tahoe transit officials investigate bus driver seen apparently dozing off on route - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Tahoe transit officials investigate bus driver seen apparently dozing off on route - NewsBreak

author: Annie Vainshtein
title: Tahoe transit officials investigate bus driver seen apparently dozing off on route - NewsBreak
text:
By Annie Vainshtein ,
8 hours ago A major transportation operator in the Tahoe area is conducting an internal investigation into one of its bus drivers after a troubling video appeared to show the man struggling to stay awake during his route.
The episode was captured on video by Jacob Greiner, a 29-year-old Placer County resident who was riding the Tahoe Truckee Area Regional Transit bus from Tahoe City to King’s Beach when he and another passenger noticed the bus driver making erratic movements and, appearing at times to slip into a brief slumber.
A major transportation operator in the Tahoe area is conducting an internal investigation into one of its bus drivers after a troubling video appeared to show the man struggling to stay awake during his route. (Courtesy Jacob Greiner) Greiner pulled out his phone and began recording. In a 78-second clip he shared with the Chronicle, the driver can be seen apparently drifting in and out of a doze, his eyes visibly fatigued in his large rearview mirror and his fingers straining to grip the steering wheel. At some points, he appears to be using the grip of his seatbelt to keep himself awake.
“I’m getting off this bus,” Greiner tells the fellow passenger. Just before the end of the video, the driver briefly nods off. The two passengers decided they’d had enough, and got off the bus at the next stop.
In a statement to the Chronicle, Chris Gray-Garcia, the communications and public affairs deputy director for Placer County said the county was aware of the incident and was conducting an internal investigation, but declined to comment on the status of the “personnel matter.”
“We take these reports and the safety of our passengers seriously,” said Gray-Garcia. “...It is our top priority to provide safe, professional, and courteous service and appropriate action will be taken.”
The video raises questions about rest time and operator fatigue for municipal bus drivers. San Francisco Municipal Transit Agency conducted at least two internal investigations over the last year after videos circulated on social media showing its drivers falling asleep at the wheel before they crashed.
In one of the videos, a Muni operator began to doze off just before his train rear-ended another train, jolting him forward and shattering the front window, the Chronicle reported. The driver was placed on a “non-driving status” while the agency conducted an official review.
Last September, a video captured a Muni train suddenly accelerating and lurching before it collided with a section of track near a city tunnel. Just before the crash, as passengers were boarding the train, the operator could be seen slumped over in her chair.
